event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: TSN’s 2024-11-12 filing explicitly connects the COVID-19 pandemic to both realized and prospective operational threats.  The company acknowledges that many parts of its business were “negatively affected” during 2020-2021, confirming that the pandemic produced direct, material impacts on operations.  It also lists forward-looking vulnerabilities—higher health-and-safety costs, supply-chain volatility, labour shortages and rising raw-material and freight costs—indicating that pandemic-driven disruptions remain a live strategic risk.  The language is largely qualitative: no dollar amounts or margin impacts are provided, and some phrasing is boiler-plate.  Nevertheless, the disclosures go beyond generic statements by identifying concrete pressure points (cost inflation, supply chain, labour).  Because the first wave of COVID-19 began in March 2020—roughly 4 ½ years before the filing—Time-Decay places the evidence in the “medium-term” bucket (4-10 years), capping maximum snippet scores at 6.  Sentences describing historic impacts receive the highest allowable scores (6) because they confirm actual harm, whereas purely forward-looking or umbrella statements are scored lower (1-4).  No mitigating language (e.g., pandemic contingency plans or insurance coverage) is supplied, so deductions are minimal.  Overall, the risk profile is moderate but credible and persistent, meriting mid-range severity scores across the extracted evidence.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic, many parts of our business and operations were negatively affected.

components.reason: Explicit link to COVID-19 (named event) with direct statement of negative impact.
Past-tense confirmation that the impact actually occurred, not merely hypothetical.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, realized harm from COVID-19 warrants the maximum medium-term score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Negative effects from a global pandemic could include an increase in operating costs in connection with higher costs associated with protecting the health and safety of team members.

components.reason: Identifies specific cost category (health-and-safety operating costs) as at risk.
Forward-looking (‘could include’) indicates potential rather than realized impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies a future cost pressure but is hypothetical, so mid-range score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: If there is a pandemic, we may also experience disruption and volatility in our supply chain, which could result in increased costs for certain raw materials, packaging materials and transportation costs.

components.reason: Highlights supply-chain disruption and multiple cost categories (raw materials, packaging, transport).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Details possible supply-chain and cost risks; hypothetical nature keeps score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, our operations, or those of producers who provide live animals to our production operations, may become more limited in their ability to procure, deliver, or produce our food products because of labor shortages.

components.reason: Connects pandemic-induced labour shortages to curtailed production/procurement capacity.
Uses conditional ‘may’, indicating prospective risk rather than certain impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies critical labour-supply vulnerability; prospective wording caps score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Global pandemics have had, and may in the future have, an adverse impact on our business and operations.

components.reason: General acknowledgement of past and future adverse impact from pandemics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic statement of impact without specifics earns a low-moderate score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Global pandemics, or localized epidemics, have had and may in the future have an adverse impact on our business and operations.

components.reason: Repeats generic acknowledgment of pandemic risk but adds epidemics; no new specifics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Redundant, broadly-phrased risk mention merits minimal score (1).

evidence_list.snippet: Natural disasters, fire, pandemic or extreme weather, could impair the health or growth of livestock or interfere with our operations due to power outages, fuel shortages, decrease in availability of water, damage to our production and processing facilities or disruption of transportation channels or unfavorably impact the demand for, or our consumers’ ability to purchase our products, among other things.

components.reason: Lists pandemic among several catastrophic risks with operational consequences (livestock health, facility damage, demand).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pandemic is bundled with other hazards; generic framing keeps score modest at 2.
